reuse.why: Replaces the four inline midpoint copies with a new shared getExpectedAmount, makes getScheduledAmount delegate to it and reuses getApproxNumberThreshold, but the API field calls getScheduledAmount without the op so approximate amounts there skip the shared approx rule.

duplication.why: The midpoint copies are removed, but the forecast, posting, preview and updateActions sites keep their own `== null ? 0 :` dispatch that getScheduledAmount already does, and the template keeps its own isbetween/isapprox op dispatch around the helper.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts next to getScheduledAmount; the API field is added in the existing scheduleModel mapper.

scope.why: Focused on the amount rule and API field, though four release notes are added for one cumulative change and getWorstCaseAmount is exported only as a trivial Math.min wrapper.

maintainability.why: Two overlapping entry points (getScheduledAmount and getExpectedAmount) plus a one-line getWorstCaseAmount, stale 'furthest from zero' comments at the call sites, and op threaded inconsistently (API model and Balance omit it) make it easy to diverge.

bypasses_abstraction.where: scheduleModel.toExternal and Balance.tsx call getScheduledAmount without the op, so the isapprox rule is skipped; schedule-template.ts decides which ops go through the helper itself.

disguised_duplication.where: The residual null and op dispatches are leftovers of the old inline code rather than reshaped copies of the new rule.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gained an `op` parameter and getExpectedAmount an isapprox branch; api-models.ts scheduleModel.toExternal and desktop-client Balance.tsx call the helper without op, and schedule-template.ts keeps its own op filter around getExpectedAmount.
